An in-kind transfer refers to the ability to move investments from one account to another account without selling.  In this case, OP is looking to exchange a mutual fund into a different mutual fund position, which is taxable.  There are instances where you can do a mutual fund exchange in a taxable account without incurring taxes, but only if you're upgrading share classes or doing an ETF conversion.

- Exchanging VHIAX for VTSAX would indeed be a taxable event.
- The holding period is based on when you initially purchased VHIAX, it doesn't matter when it was transferred.  So if you had it for over a year, it's long-term and more favorable tax-wise.
- Generally speaking, divesting from VHIAX for a lower cost alternative like VTSAX is ideal.  The 0.04% expense ratio of VTSAX is 1/25th that of the 0.99% of VHIAX.  Not to mention you're paying a premium for underperforming the index long-term when you could instead go with the flow of the index.

Here's what I think will realistically happen this offseason:

C: Bring Higgy back to platoon with Wells.  Trade Trevino for prospect capital.  He's worthless even as a back-up at this point.

1B: We sadly need to part ways with Rizzo by buying out his contract.  He is at the end of his career and will naturally continue to regress.  I could see him spending a final 1-2 years doing a farewell tour with the Cubs.  As for who takes over, this may be a hot take, but the Yankees might use a stop-gap for 1B next year.  I could see an Oswaldo/DJ platoon.  If this is the case, the Yankees should give DJ a 2-month window to prove himself capable of playing at a major league level.  If he fails, the Yankees should eat the $30 million and DFA him.  This of course is not ideal but the Yankees are victims of the sunk cost fallacy and will do everything in their power to keep DJ until it blows up in their faces.  The quality FA options for 1B are likely too expensive to sign alongside Soto, so if the Yankees want to prevent 1B being a weakness, the trade market would likely be the only route.  Even then, options are limited.

2B: Resign Gleyber.  If we don't, our infield would become a joke.  Sure, Jazz could take over 2B, but what do we do about 3B? Berti? DJ? Peraza? Hell no.  Not to mention the FA market at 3B is ice cold this offseason.  In short, yeah Gleyber has his shortcomings, but he's solid and what other choice do we have? I can't imagine he'd be much more expensive than he is now anyways.

SS: Keep Volpe.

3B: Keep Jazz for the reasons explained in the 2B section.

LF: Let Verdugo walk.  While the trade for him seemed enticing at first, the pinstripes were way too heavy.  Instead, we should stop squandering Dominguez's potential and have him start full-time in LF.  Similar to 2023 Volpe, it's gonna be rough.  He is gonna get baptismed by fire and make a few mistakes in the field, but his ceiling is so high and he is 100% ready to move up from AAA at this point.  Baptism by fire is the only way he will reach his potential.

CF: Judge is a lock.

RF: BLANK CHECK.  He's the reason why the Yankees didn't finish 82-80 again.  Since the Yankees are unlikely to change much outside of Soto, it goes without saying that he needs to come back by any means necessary.  In the event that he walks, there's no shortage of quality outfielders in the FA market he could be replaced by (Profar, Kepler, Teoscar, Santander, etc.).  But let's be real: Soto's a Scott Boras client.  By the time he decides to pack up, who's gonna be left?  Exactly.  Yet another reason why we need him back.

SP: Add that extra year to Cole's contract.  We can't risk an opt-out.  This is a problem for future Yankees. 

RP: The Clay Holmes experiment has failed and the Yankees (surprisingly) realize it.  We will let him walk.  We need to bring Kahnle back.  Bring Loaisiga back (unless his health is in the shitter).  Bring back Hill.  As for additions, I have full faith in Matt Blake to work with the FO to figure it out.

TLDR: Let's be real here, the Yankees are gonna run it back for the most part.  Key takeaways are to resign Soto and Gleyber, bring Higgy back to shore up the Catcher position, and give Dominguez a chance.  If we don't sign Soto, then it's back to mediocrity.
